papers.title: Hybrid auxetics: Postponing failure with elastomer infiltration of Ti-6Al-4V lattices
papers.abstract: This work examines how a soft elastomeric phase can be used to reinforce and delay the failure of additively manufactured metal lattice structures with auxetic geometry. A novel hexaround unit-cell was designed to ensure printability of Ti-6Al-4V via laser powder-bed fusion. Once infiltrated with a compliant polyurethane, these hybrid lattices showed a pronounced delay in strut-level failure and shear-band formation. Microtomography coupled with in-situ compression experiments confirmed that nodal cracking commonly observed in unfilled lattices is mitigated by the polymer phase. While hybrid lattices exhibited comparable or slightly increased stiffness only at large deformations, their enhanced integrity and stress redistribution suggest promise for crashworthiness and impact applications requiring high ductility or energy absorption. We discuss how the stiffness ratio between filler and metallic skeleton determines the extent of improvement, offering design guidelines for next-generation hybrid lattices. This is the first in-situ tomographic evidence that a compliant matrix can defer the critical shear-band in an additively manufactured metal auxetic lattice. • A re-entrant auxetic lattice design improves printability via laser powder-bed fusion, balancing geometric complexity and robust manufacturability. • Elastomer infiltration helps redistribute stress, delaying nodal cracks and promoting a more controlled collapse under compressive loading. • This is the first in situ tomographic evidence that a compliant matrix can defer the critical shear-band in metal auxetic lattice. • The hybrid structure maintains better load-bearing capacity at large deformations, preserving integrity where unfilled lattices fail. • Enhanced energy absorption at high strains suggests suitability for crashworthiness applications.

summary_en.motivation: To delay failure of additively manufactured metal lattice structures by infiltrating a soft elastomeric phase.
summary_en.method: A novel hexaround unit-cell was designed for printability via LPBF; Ti-6Al-4V lattices were infiltrated with polyurethane and tested under compression with in-situ microtomography.
summary_en.result: Hybrid lattices exhibited delayed strut-level failure and shear-band formation, with mitigated nodal cracking and improved load-bearing capacity at large deformations.
summary_en.validation: In-situ compression combined with microtomography provided direct evidence of failure postponement and stress redistribution.

papers.title: Mechanical and Corrosion Properties of Ultrafine-Grained TC4-0.55Fe Alloy Processed by Equal-Channel Angular Pressing
papers.abstract: This study investigates the effects of multi-pass Equal-Channel Angular Pressing (ECAP) on the mechanical and corrosion properties of TC4-0.55Fe alloy through room-temperature tensile tests, electrochemical experiments, SEM, and EBSD characterization. The results demonstrate that, with increasing ECAP passes, the average grain size is progressively refined from the initial 3.8 μm to 1.8 μm after four passes. After four passes, the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength increase from initial values of 906 MPa and 939 MPa to 995 MPa and 1022 MPa, respectively, while the elongation at fracture slightly decreases to 12.0%. Electrochemical corrosion results reveal that ECAP processing significantly enhances the corrosion resistance of the TC4-0.55Fe alloy. Specifically, the two-pass specimen exhibits nearly an order-of-magnitude reduction in both corrosion rate and self-corrosion current density compared to the initial state. The simultaneous improvement in strength and corrosion resistance is primarily attributed to the synergistic effects of grain refinement, increased dislocation density, and the evolution of basal texture.

papers.title: Fretting Fatigue Behaviour of Laser Powder Bed Fusion- Produced Ti-6Al-4V: Experimental and Numerical Analysis

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究激光粉末床熔融Ti-6Al-4V的微动疲劳行为，属于层1基础力学与疲劳范畴，与研究方向高度相关。
llm.why_not_core: Does not cover standard uniaxial fatigue or tensile properties, focusing instead on fretting fatigue, a specialized mechanism within the fatigue scope.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究激光粉末床熔融Ti-6Al-4V的微动疲劳行为
summary_zh.method: 结合微动疲劳实验与数值模拟分析
summary_zh.result: 揭示了微动条件下的疲劳损伤机制与寿命规律
summary_zh.validation: 通过微动疲劳实验验证结果

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the fretting fatigue behavior of laser powder bed fusion-produced Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: A combined approach of experimental fretting fatigue tests and numerical modeling was employed.
summary_en.result: The damage mechanisms and fatigue life under fretting conditions were characterized.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fretting fatigue tests provided validation for numerical predictions.
